predecessors.name: Duchy of Opole
predecessors.text: Bytom, partitioned from the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz in c.

successors.name: Duchy of Opole
successors.text: the whole duchy, merged with Opole under Jan II the Good in 1498

ledger.x: c. 1281: the Duchy of Bytom is partitioned from the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz. The page says the duchy was established 'about 1281' when the Duchy of Opole and Racibórz was split among the sons of Władysław Opolski; the Casimir page puts Władysław's death in 1282 and the formal division in 1284.
1284: Casimir takes Bytom with Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice and Siewierz.
1355: the Bytom Piast line dies out and the duchy passes to other Piast houses.
1498: the Duchy of Bytom is merged back into the Duchy of Opole under Jan II the Good.
1498: end of the Duchy of Bytom, merged with Opole.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given on either page; the duchy is a set of named towns (Bytom, Koźle, Toszek, Gliwice, Siewierz) and the borders are approximate throughout.
